constitution.gameplay_identity: large 23rd-century Starfleet exploration/cruiser platform with strong diplomacy, science, patrol and defense utility
constraints: dated_configuration_must_match_campaign_year
crew_and_internal_layout_may_change_substantially_by_configuration
major_refit_is_explicit_event_not_cosmetic_skin
crew_generation: derive departments from installed systems and mission
reference complement is guidance, not a random population target
persistence: same individual vessel persists through compatible refit
ai_boundary: AI may describe known class capabilities but cannot invent live readiness, damage, crew or unsourced exact performance.

constraints: do_not_assume_one_identical_mission_configuration
late-era examples may be veteran/refitted designs
persistence: configuration/refit history belongs to individual ship
old hull does not imply poor maintenance automatically
ai_boundary: Do not infer armament, sensor fit or internal layout beyond selected configuration.
visual_hooks: shared Miranda silhouette with configuration/refit differences

excelsior.gameplay_identity: late-23rd-century cruiser/explorer with very long 24th-century fleet-service relevance
constraints: prototype/early service and later mature configurations must be date-aware
age alone does not imply obsolescence in all systems
crew_generation: mission and dated configuration drive staffing
persistence: refits can extend service without creating new identity
ai_boundary: Do not use registry sequence as chronology or infer exact refit level from class name.
visual_hooks: era-sensitive nacelle/hull/refit detail only when sourced

constraints: not a generic frontline combatant
exact tactical capacity remains configuration-specific
crew_generation: science specialists can dominate mission complement
smaller watch structure than large explorers
ai_boundary: Do not inflate combat capability because player importance is high.
visual_hooks: mission equipment additions need explicit configuration

constraints: large crew/population produces major logistics and social simulation load
saucer separation is capability not default behavior
crew_generation: civilian/passenger population remains separate from duty crew
persistence: saucer/stardrive states remain same ship identity unless explicit catastrophic separation outcome defines otherwise
ai_boundary: Do not treat approximately 1000 aboard as 1000 duty officers; do not invent current civilian complement.
visual_hooks: saucer separation only from authoritative state

nebula.gameplay_identity: 24th-century multi-mission Starfleet platform with configurable mission emphasis
constraints: specific mission module/configuration must be resolved before assuming specialist capability
persistence: module changes require explicit refit/configuration event
ai_boundary: Do not assume every Nebula carries identical mission hardware.

intrepid.gameplay_identity: 2370s long-range explorer optimized for science, speed and relatively lean crew
constraints: technology availability is late-24th-century only
EMH presence/capability does not imply persistent holographic personhood
crew_generation: leaner complement increases cross-qualification and vacancy consequences
persistence: bio-neural damage/repairs and EMH state are individual ship state
ai_boundary: Do not equate Intrepid class with Voyager's unique campaign history or exact loadout.

constraints: small size/crew limits broad long-duration support compared with explorers
cloaking device is not generic class capability
crew_generation: small crew makes casualties/vacancies immediately consequential
persistence: individual special equipment such as cloak belongs to ship configuration and political authorization
ai_boundary: Never assume cloak because class=Defiant; never copy USS Defiant special history into generated class members.
visual_hooks: special equipment only if configuration says so

sovereign.gameplay_identity: advanced late-24th-century Starfleet long-range capital starship balancing exploration, diplomacy and very strong defensive/tactical capability
constraints: not available before late-24th-century introduction
class capability does not imply permanent combat posture
individual Enterprise-E history and damage are never class defaults
exact complement and internal arrangement remain configuration-specific unless sourced
crew_generation: mission profile determines tactical, science, diplomatic and support staffing
civilian/passenger presence is individual-assignment state rather than automatic class population
persistence: refits, damage, registry, command crew and mission equipment belong to the individual ship
generated Sovereign-class vessels remain persistent identities once materialized
ai_boundary: Do not infer USS Enterprise-E-specific officers, history, damage, modifications or readiness from class identity.
AI may describe established class-level capabilities but cannot invent live tactical status.
visual_hooks: long secondary hull integrated with broad forward saucer
individual registry and damage overlays only from authoritative state

generation_rules: Filter by date, operator, role and configuration before class selection.
Veteran classes remain valid where canon supports continued service.
Player importance never forces prestigious or newest class.
Generated individual ships receive stable ship_id and persist once materialized.
Class data never contains individual damage, crew, captain or live readiness.
unknown_policy: Exact unsourced deck counts, complements, performance figures and internal layouts remain unknown/configuration-specific.
nap_implications: NAP binds exterior assets first to class/design and dated configuration, then to individual ship identity and current state.
